title: Counting Toward New Year
description: Mark a year-end gathering through familiar clock parts, time units, and celebration words.
cardDescription: Mark a year-end gathering through familiar clock parts, time units, and celebration words.
focus: The clues combine timekeeping with ordinary actions at a gathering. Some words have a special social meaning.
solvingTip: Look for a time unit, a clock feature, or a celebratory action.
words: Time marking the start of a new calendar day
Device displaying the passage of time
Time unit making up one-sixtieth of a minute
Moving pointer on an analog clock
Musical ringing sound made by a clock
Ringing instrument sounded to mark an occasion
Expression of goodwill made while raising a drink
Joyful shout at a shared celebration
Hope expressed for the coming year
Calendar period divided into twelve months
Arrangement showing days, weeks, and months

answerNotes.HAND: Hand is a clock pointer in this clue. It does not mean a body part.
answerNotes.TOAST: Toast names a spoken gesture of goodwill here. It is not browned bread.
answerNotes.MIDNIGHT: Midnight is the boundary between calendar days. It differs from noon, the middle of daylight hours by clock convention.
answerNotes.CALENDAR: A calendar organizes dates. A clock measures and displays time within a day.

title: A Valentine on the Table
description: Explore a friendly February greeting through familiar messages, flowers, and gift details.
cardDescription: Explore a friendly February greeting through familiar messages, flowers, and gift details.
focus: The clues describe objects and considerate actions. Direct meanings identify the words without song lyrics or literary quotations.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue asks for a message, a decorative object, or an action.
words: Familiar symbol of affection drawn on a Valentine
Written greeting offered for Valentine’s Day
Paper covering holding a mailed Valentine
Postage label attached before mailing a card
Flower traditionally associated with a romantic gift
Decorative strip tied around a February gift
Looped knot decorating a small present
Cacao-based sweet often given in an assortment
Person known with warmth and trust
Deep affection expressed in a personal greeting
Considerate treatment shown toward another person
Short personal message inside a card
To add one’s name to a Valentine
To let another person have part of a gift or treat

answerNotes.HEART: Heart names the drawn symbol here. The clue does not ask about the physical organ.
answerNotes.NOTE: Note is a written message in this setting. It is not one musical pitch.
answerNotes.SIGN: Sign is an action meaning add a name. It differs from a printed marker or road notice.
answerNotes.BOW: Bow names the looped ribbon knot. It rhymes with go in this gift setting.

title: A St. Patrick’s Day Procession
description: Meet familiar Irish-themed symbols, instruments, and parade words.
cardDescription: Meet familiar Irish-themed symbols, instruments, and parade words.
focus: The clues describe cultural images and ordinary procession objects. They identify names without requiring historical dates.
solvingTip: Look for a plant symbol, an instrument, or something seen in a parade.
words: Three-leaf sprig traditionally associated with Ireland
Small plant whose leaves commonly have three leaflets
Color strongly associated with St. Patrick’s Day displays
One flat plant part in a clover sprig
Slender support beneath a plant’s leaves
String instrument used as an Irish national symbol
Violin heard in traditional Irish music
Group of musicians taking part in a procession
To walk in step with a procession
Decorative strip worn or tied for an occasion
Head covering decorated for a seasonal celebration
Good fortune wished for in a familiar greeting
Country associated with shamrock and harp symbols

answerNotes.SHAMROCK: A shamrock is traditionally a three-leaf sprig. It is not the same idea as the four-leaf clover associated with luck.
answerNotes.HARP: The harp is an Irish cultural symbol. The clue asks for the instrument rather than its player.
answerNotes.FIDDLE: Fiddle is a name for the violin in a traditional-music setting. It does not necessarily identify a different instrument.
answerNotes.CLOVER: Clover leaves commonly have three leaflets. A leaflet is one division of the compound leaf.

title: A Fourth of July Picnic
description: Picture a familiar summer celebration through flags, processions, picnic foods, and decorative lights.
cardDescription: Picture a familiar summer celebration through flags, processions, picnic foods, and decorative lights.
focus: The clues describe a community gathering in the United States. Objects and shapes provide the answers rather than historical trivia.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names a symbol, a food, a procession item, or a light effect.
words: Fabric symbol flown for a national celebration
Long narrow band appearing on the U.S. flag
Pointed symbol in the U.S. flag’s blue field
Organized procession held for a community occasion
Musicians playing together in a holiday procession
To walk in an ordered procession
Meal enjoyed outdoors during a summer celebration
Long display sign carried through a street
Inflated decorative object at a gathering
Outdoor cooking surface at a summer picnic
Cob-grown food commonly served at a cookout
Large juicy summer fruit often served in wedges
Small bright flashing point of light
Display item producing a bright pyrotechnic effect

answerNotes.STRIPE: A stripe is a long band of color. Its shape distinguishes it from a separate star symbol.
answerNotes.STAR: Star names a flag symbol here. It does not refer to a distant sun in this clue.
answerNotes.BANNER: A banner carries a displayed message or design. It differs from the musicians forming a band.
answerNotes.WATERMELON: A watermelon is a large fruit often cut into wedges. The clue uses its familiar serving form rather than one named variety.

title: A Birthday Gathering
description: Set a birthday table through familiar greetings, gifts, serving words, and decorations.
cardDescription: Set a birthday table through familiar greetings, gifts, serving words, and decorations.
focus: The clues identify objects and roles at a celebration. Some words name what is served, while others name what is written or displayed.
solvingTip: Look for a greeting, a decoration, a food portion, or a person’s role.
words: Sweet baked centerpiece of a birthday table
Small wax light placed on a birthday cake
Hope traditionally made during a birthday celebration
Written greeting offered for a birthday
Present given to mark a personal occasion
Looped ribbon knot on a birthday parcel
Rigid container holding a birthday gift
Long displayed sign carrying a birthday greeting
Person invited to a birthday gathering
Person welcoming people to a celebration
One cut serving of a birthday cake
Period added when another birthday is reached

answerNotes.CANDLE: A candle is the whole wax light. The flame is the burning light at its top.
answerNotes.GUEST: Guest names the invited role. It does not specify how the person is related to the host.
answerNotes.HOST: The host welcomes the gathering. The word identifies a role rather than the celebration itself.
answerNotes.SLICE: Slice is a noun for a served piece here. It can also be the action of cutting such a piece.
